title: PTL Health — Project ignition & ops intake
summary: Initial implementation intake and ops alignment for PTL Health's rollout of Redwood Inference in a VPC/private deployment. Covered architecture constraints, compliance needs (SOC2/ISO), SSO/KMS integration, and pilot success criteria. Agreed next steps for environment access, benchmark plan, and a security doc handoff.
topics: deployment mode: private VPC vs dedicated
KMS/HSM key management and encryption at rest
next_steps: Redwood to share PRD + VPC checklist and security pack (Samantha) by 2026-08-06
PTL to provide test dataset and sample traffic profile (Priya) by 2026-08-10
Schedule private deployment walkthrough and baseline benchmark the week of 2026-08-17 (Daniel / Marcus)
action_items: Samantha: send security pack + SOC2 artifacts link — due 2026-08-06
Priya: upload anonymized sample logs and traffic matrix to shared drive — due 2026-08-10
Daniel: prepare benchmark script template and ops runbook draft — due 2026-08-14
transcript:
Meeting header: PTL Health - Project ignition & ops intake
Date/Time: 2026-08-03 17:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samantha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Marcus (Redwood SE), Oliver (PTL Head of ML), Priya (PTL Platform), Rashida (PTL CTO), Evan (PTL Security)

Summary (auto): quick intake to align on network, security, and pilot criteria. Rough consensus on private VPC deployment with option to evaluate Dedicated later. Need SSO/SAML and KMS details; Redwood to share security pack and follow up with benchmarking plan.

[00:00] Samantha: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. quick intros then we'll jump into the ops intake and constraints. I'm Samantha, AE on the account, Daniel and Marcus from the SE team are here, Lina is your CSM.
[00:15] Oliver: hey all, Oliver here. we'll be leading the ML side, Priya is our platform eng and will do the access stuff, Rashida is our CTO and Evan is security. thanks.
[00:27] Daniel: great, thanks. real quick agenda, 1) network and deployment model, 2) compliance and keys, 3) pilot success criteria and benchmarks, 4) next steps. anything to add?
[00:38] Priya: maybe just to mention we have some egress rules and we run in a restricted VPC, so the deployment has to conform to no public IPs ideally. also we use private link for most cloud services.
[00:50] Marcus: noted, we have a private deployment option that supports VPC endpoints and on-prem connectors. we can run the control plane out-of-band if you need, or provide a customer-managed control plane.
[01:05] Rashida: clarify that — you mean the control plane still needs to reach Redwood? we have an air-gapped-ish requirement, so prefer no outbound calls to third-party unless authenticated through our proxy.
[01:18] Daniel: yeah, so two patterns we see — 1) fully private with a customer-managed control plane and local ops, or 2) a split model where the control plane has limited endpoints to Redwood for telemetry and billing. both are possible, but the split model needs explicit allow lists and a proxy.
[01:35] Evan: from security perspective, minimal outbound, everything over TLS, mTLS optional, and KMS integration is a hard requirement. we need to ensure keys never leave our HSM.
[01:47] Samantha: understoood. we have integrations for KMS and HSM, we support customer-managed keys and can integrate with common providers — AWS KMS, Azure, GCP KMS, and HSMs via KMIP. we'll include our KMS integration diagram in the pack.
[02:00] Oliver: also SOC 2 and ISO reports — do you have those available to share?
[02:06] Lina: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts — i'll include the redacted reports in the security pack.
[02:14] Priya: great. on networking, we need NAT control and strict egress, can your installer be run from bastion hosts only? sometimes installers try to reach public endpoints on first boot.
[02:26] Marcus: installer can be run via an air-gapped bundle, we have an offline package, or we can run with a staged container registry inside your private network. there are a few options depending on your infra team preference.
[02:40] [02:40] Oliver: okay that helps. next, can we talk about the runtime — we're really sensitive to latency for inference, targets are 90th percentile under 120ms for short-form generation on seq length ~128 tokens.
[02:55] Daniel: that's reasonable, do you have expected QPS?
[02:59] Oliver: around 8-12 QPS steady, spikes to 30 during batch jobs.
[03:05] Daniel: okay good. our serving runtime supports continuous batching and prefix/KV cache — though sometimes the transcript here says K-V cash, but it's KV cache — that should help cost and throughput. for your 90th pctl target we might need a mix of instance types and maybe a quantized variant.
[03:22] Priya: about quantization, we do want to preserve output quality — we have downstream regulatory checks, so any model degradation must be measured. what tooling do you have for evals?
[03:33] Marcus: we ship an eval harness and a playground for A/B tests. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles based on a benchmark run. we'll produce quality regression alerts tied to a prompt set you supply.
[03:46] Rashida: is that integrated into the console? can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns?
[03:51] Daniel: yes — the Redwood Console offers per-model and per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and traces. for private deployments we can run the telemetry to the customer console, or redact data and send metrics to your telemetry stack.
[04:06] Evan: encryption at rest — we require that model artifacts and logs are encrypted with our CMK and audit logs retained for 7 years. can you support that retention?
[04:16] Samantha: audit log retention is configurable; we typically support long retention windows for enterprise accounts. we'll confirm retention policy limits in the security pack.
[04:25] [04:25] Priya: about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta with SAML + SCIM provisioning, want per-team roles, and audit trails.
[04:35] Lina: that's supported. we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles in the console, and you can apply route-level permissions. we'll include a sample SCIM mapping file.
[04:44] Oliver: excellent. this is mostly alignment. next is pilot acceptance criteria — we want three things: stability for two weeks under production-like load, P95 latency below 200ms, and functional parity with our current model outputs within an L2 norm threshold. does that map to what you normally sign off on?
[05:00] Daniel: yes that's in line. i'd add that we'll run a regression suite against your golden prompt set and produce a report. for stability we'll propose a canary rollout and gradual traffic increase to avoid cold-start spikes.
[05:12] Marcus: also planning for automatic fallback policies in case of degraded performance — we can route traffic to a lower-latency variant or to a cached response.
[05:22] Priva: little interjection — how do you handle KV cache invalidation across replicas? we've seen cache inconsistency cause stale completions.
[05:30] Daniel: good question. our runtime coordinates KV cache with a sharded architecture and consistent hashing; invalidations happen via sequence tags. i know that sounds a bit like 'K-V cash' in notes, apologies for the mis-scribe. we'll include a diagram in the ops runbook.
[05:46] Rashida: OK. procurement question — do you require a dedicated reserved capacity purchase up front? or can we start hosted and then move to private?
[05:55] Samantha: you can start with hosted API for evaluation, but given your data residency and security needs, private is the recommended path. Dedicated reserved capacity is available for predictable throughput — we can propose a hybrid pilot to limit spend initially.
[06:10] Evan: any compliance scoping around data residency? some of our PHI flows must stay within region.
[06:17] Samantha: region pinning is supported in private and dedicated. we'll need to map your data flows to confirm.
[06:24] Oliver: okay good. let's talk timeline — we aim to run a pilot in September, production by November. realistic?
[06:33] Daniel: yes, plausible. immediate blockers are providing access to a staging VPC and test data. if we get that by mid-August, we can land a baseline benchmark the week of Aug 17th and iterate.
[06:45] Priya: we'll need a list of required IAM roles and ports. can you send a checklist?
[06:51] Marcus: yes, we'll send a VPC/network checklist and an install runbook.
[06:56] [06:56] Oliver: one more — are you able to do a short POC where we run our model artifacts, not your curated model? we want to keep our weights private.
[07:06] Samantha: absolutely, the platform supports customer-supplied model artifacts and you can pin versions. for the pilot we can run with your model in a private registry.
[07:15] Evan: ok on data access controls — logs should be segmented per-tenant and we need RBAC for ops engineers.
[07:22] Lina: we'll map roles to tenants and set up audit streams. also want to note that our support SLA tiers include 24/7 on-call for production incidents if you select enterprise support.
[07:34] Rashida: what's the pricing model for the pilot? approximate numbers are fine.
[07:40] Samantha: for pilots we often do a time-limited blended rate plus usage. for Dedicated we have reserved capacity contracts. i'll send a ballpark estimate in the follow-up, but figure per-token and per-embedding units for hosted, and committed GPU hours for Dedicated.
[07:55] Priya: fine. also want to coordinate bench metrics — can you provide a benchmark harness that runs latency p95/p99 and token-level cost?
[08:05] Daniel: yes, we'll share a benchmark script that runs sequence-length sweeps and produces CSV outputs you can drop into your dashboards. it measures p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, tokens-per-second, and cost estimates.
[08:18] Oliver: great. are there any gotchas we should know about? like hidden egress or telemetry that might leak data?
[08:26] Marcus: default telemetry is metadata-only; payloads can be excluded in private deployments. we'll make sure the telemetry does not include prompt/response content unless explicitly enabled for debugging.
[08:39] [08:39] Priya: if we're doing tenant isolation, can we run different model variants per team?
[08:44] Daniel: yes, you can pin models per-route and per-tenant, and set rollouts for canaries.
[08:50] Rashida: ok I'm satisfied high level. next questions from legal/procurement will be around indemnity and data processing addendum, we'll have that team reach out.
[08:59] Samantha: of course, we have standard DPAs and can work with your legal team. I'll loop in our contracts lead in the follow-up.
[09:07] Evan: small question — how do you handle model updates and patching for security CVEs?
[09:12] Marcus: we maintain rolling patch policies for the serving runtime, with scheduled maintenance windows. for model security, we provide guidance and can pin to vetted model versions; we also support air-gapped updates via signed artifacts.
[09:25] Priya: timeline and milestone recap would be helpful.
[09:29] Samantha: agreed. here are the proposed milestones: 1) security pack + VPC checklist (Redwood) by Aug 6; 2) PTL provides sample data and staging VPC access by Aug 10; 3) Redwood runs baseline benchmark week of Aug 17; 4) pilot run Sept 1-14; 5) production readiness review early Oct. does that align?
[09:51] Oliver: yes that's fine.
[09:53] Rashida: approved tentatively.
[09:55] Daniel: quick follow-up on benchmarks — do you have a golden prompt set for regression tests or should we collaborate on creating one?
[10:03] Oliver: we have a gold set internally but it's messy; we'll share a sanitized subset.
[10:08] Priya: note that the traffic profile includes bursty loads from end-of-day reports and nightly batch jobs. we'll include that in the traffic matrix.
[10:16] Marcus: perfect. we'll simulate those peaks in the benchmark harness.
[10:20] [10:20] Lina: anything else we should capture as risks? I'm noting: dependency on staging VPC access, potential delays on SOC review, and the need for signed model artifacts if air-gapped. any others?
[10:32] Evan: also vendor indemnity around PHI, so legal will take a look.
[10:36] Samantha: we'll provide a redacted SOC2, our DPA, and a checklist. I'll also include a sample SAML/SCIM config.
[10:44] Oliver: sounds good. last one — will there be a central Slack / shared channel for ops comms?
[10:49] Lina: yes we'll create a shared Slack channel and a Confluence space for runbooks.
[10:55] Samantha: ok let's recap.
[11:00] Recap: Redwood to send security pack + VPC checklist + SOC2 artifacts (Samantha/Lina) by Aug 6; PTL provides staging VPC details and sanitized prompt set (Priya/Oliver) by Aug 10; Redwood to run baseline benchmark and share results week of Aug 17 (Daniel/Marcus); schedule private deployment walkthrough — proposed Aug 19 (all).
[11:23] Oliver: good. thanks everyone.
[11:26] Rashida: thanks.
[11:28] Samantha: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with docs and calendar invites.
[11:33] [END]
